chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, all from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Furat ibn Ahnaf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Any believer who withholds from a believer something that he needs, while he is able to provide it from his own possession or from that of others, Allah will make him stand on the Day of Judgment with a blackened face, his eyes blue, his hands tied to his neck, and it will be said: 'This is the betrayer who betrayed Allah and His Messenger.' Then he will be commanded to be taken to the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a believer who withholds help from another believer when they are able to give?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a definitive warning against selfishness, emphasizing that withholding even minor benefits while having the capacity to give constitutes a breach of covenant with Allah and the Prophet. The vivid eschatological imagery of the blackened face and bound hands serves as a physical manifestation of spiritual failure, reinforcing the Shia concept of *ittisal* (connection) among believers through mutual support. This narration underscores the practical implication that faith is validated not just by belief, but by the active removal of barriers to another's well-being.
